gen-dafont-neon-fs-paquito: Neon draws every letter with a pipe-cleaner line, tall lowercase stamped like metal type. Paquito's classic serif shapes keep caps and lowercase close in height, so paragraphs read with a confident, friendly ease.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded reads warm, with curves that refuse to close. Neon up top is all glowing, uniform line and tall stamped-metal lowercase, while the sans below packs its letters into thin cracks of space.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-supreme: Supreme sets a thick, heavy-looking strip of text through the middle of the line. Supreme, a sans-serif, stays crisp and open beside Neon, which has no hairlines anywhere, and that shared sturdiness is the whole appeal.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab reads dignified and refined, its classic serif caps hugging the lowercase. Neon's tube-like strokes glow like real glass tubing, and the sturdy text beneath gives that brightness something solid to stand on.
gen-dafont-neon-general-sans: Neon glows in tall, stamped-metal lowercase with open spacing. General Sans keeps steady pen pressure with an x-height that fills the line, so a full page of text moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-neon-montserrat: Vibrant glow, courtesy of Neon. Montserrat, a sans-serif, runs geometric and approachable, its oversized e and a counters gliding under the eye like wire, and that smoothness is what holds the pair together.
gen-dafont-neuropol-archivo: A slim channel at the c's opening and one fixed nib width make Neuropol look digital. Archivo, with outward-opening curves and a commanding lowercase, handles the reading while Neuropol just sets the mood.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-hoover: Futuristic is the first word, thanks to Neuropol's slim c channel and monoline stems running into serifs. Hoover's classic serif shapes, with compressed ascenders and a generous e, give paragraphs a refined, sturdy cadence.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-roundo: Digital in spirit, Neuropol keeps a slim channel at the c and a single-weight outline feel, with letters mostly closed. Roundo's plain sans letters open every small counter and handle the reading.
gen-dafont-neuropol-outfit: Outfit reads clean and approachable, its curves finishing well before they close, like cable bent into shapes. Neuropol, with its closed letters, handles the futuristic flair, while the plain sans carries the reading.
